description: Portable processor scenarios for the OpenAPI 3.0 binding-specification sibling. Configuration is named semantically; adapters normalize HTTP observations.

scenarios.description: A scalar query parameter uses the OpenAPI-declared query location and serialization rather than becoming a body field. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]
The first patch-looking edition beyond the accepted OpenAPI 3.0 set is refused rather than inferred compatible.

An OAS 3.0 binary schema carries exact raw bytes for a concrete image media type; the lane is schema-driven rather than restricted to application/octet-stream. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]
A non-canonical Base64 boundary value for an OAS 3.0 raw body refuses before dispatch. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]
Raw-body bytes are declaration-selected and never sniffed as JSON merely because their decoded spelling is JSON text. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]
A required raw body with no caller input refuses before dispatch like every other required request body.
An OAS 3.0 binary success response crosses the protocol-independent output boundary as canonical Base64 of its exact octets.

A dynamic form object is the envelope's one body value, independently of a same-named query parameter; no declaration trigger changes caller correspondence. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]
An exact schema-omitted OAS 3.0 non-JSON declaration carries request and response octets through the canonical Base64 application boundary. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]

OAS 3.0.4 is the edition where the 3.0 line first states the content interpretation ("The absence of all three of those fields is the equivalent of using content") and where Appendix E first appears. An urlencoded property with no Encoding Object therefore takes the content path there, which the OAS pairs with RFC 1866 Section 8.2.1, whose first escaping step replaces a space with +. OAS 3.0.0-3.0.3 state neither sentence and this specification states no path-selection rule for that line, so no scenario pins it. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]

expected.description: The 3.0 line reaches the content path from 3.0.4 onward. One permitted observation, not a set.

scenarios.description: On the 3.0 line no accepted edition states a default contentType row that reaches a part declaring no `type` — 3.0.0 through 3.0.3 enumerate a string with format binary, other primitive types, object, and array without a catch-all, and 3.0.4 tabulates the same cases keyed on a declared type — and openbindings.openapi-3.0@1 authors no row for that residue. The single missing fact is one media type, so the part's content type is the required `propertyMedia` configuration point, keyed by the part's property name: a required body carrying such a part challenges CONTEXT_REQUIRED (config.value, point propertyMedia, path /profile) before input consumption and dispatches nothing. This scenario pinned the specification's own value-keyed convention until 2026-08-20 (the supplied value's JSON type chose the part default), then a flat pre-dispatch refusal after escalation M2 deleted that convention; the revision-is-not-a-roadmap ruling replaced the refusal with the rung-3 answer the deference order ranks above it, since the authority is genuinely silent here rather than answering. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]

The whole OAS 3.0 line emits ONE body for a control-free urlencoded property, and this scenario is edition 3.0.0 of the five that state it. The Encoding Object writes contentType and no style, explode or allowReserved, so the content path governs: the object's JSON image rides as one field under the property's own name, with its space spelled + by RFC 1866 Section 8.2.1. Edition 3.0.0 states no lane-selection rule of its own; it reaches this behaviour through its own Section 4.1 patch-uniformity instruction together with 3.0.4, a 3.0.* version, whose Section 4.7.15.1.2 states that with all three fields absent "Encoding is to be based on contentType alone". A processor that keys any part of this on the PATCH component of the openapi field emits address's members as top-level fields (street=main%20st), discards the artifact's explicit contentType, and loses the field name the operation is built around; each of 3.0.0 through 3.0.3 forbids that distinction in its OWN Section 4.1, in the words "The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by tooling, making no distinction between 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 for example" — 3.0.4 and the 3.1 editions carry the same sentence naming 3.1.0 and 3.1.1 instead, so the instruction governing an artifact that declares a 3.0-line patch is the one in that artifact's own edition. One permitted observation, not a set. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]

scenarios.description: On the 3.0 line patternProperties is outside the Schema Object dialect and decides as if absent, while CO30-03 independently makes the envelope body the complete caller value without any dialect-keyed correspondence trigger. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]

On the 3.0 line if, dependentSchemas, and unevaluatedProperties are outside the Schema Object dialect and decide as if absent, while CO30-03 independently makes the envelope body the complete caller value without making correspondence dialect-dependent. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]

On the 3.0 line a `type: string` with `format: byte` is ALREADY the encoded characters — every accepted 3.0 edition's own Data Types format registry defines `byte` as "base64 encoded characters", 3.0.4's row citing [RFC 4648] Section 4 — so an exact non-JSON, non-form selection governed by that declaration carries the caller's string as artifact-encoded Base64 text, sent AS-IS. The OpenBindings raw-byte boundary decode does not run: artifact encoding and the OpenBindings boundary encoding are distinct, exactly as they are for the 3.1 `contentEncoding` lane this rule parallels. The lane is not gated on character-data media — application/pdf is outside that test — because here the ARTIFACT, not the media-type registration, is what declares the value to be characters. The wire body is therefore the string itself and not the three octets it encodes. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]

The form-part half of the same 3.0 cell, and its part default. 3.0.4's Encoding Object default-`contentType` table gives `string` with `format` "`binary` or `byte`" the default application/octet-stream, while 3.0.0 through 3.0.3's prose names only `binary` before "other primitive types"; under the editions' own Section 4.1 patch-uniformity instruction the line answers uniformly and 3.0.4 read under its own text fixes what the uniform answer is, so a `byte` part defaults to application/octet-stream on every 3.0 edition rather than to the primitive text/plain row. Its value is the caller's artifact-encoded Base64 text sent as-is — the contrast with the `binary` sibling, which takes the SAME default Content-Type while its value is the OpenBindings canonical Base64 boundary and emits the decoded octets, is carried by the shared format-byte-carriage case table rather than here, because one multipart body containing both parts cannot assert which part a Content-Type belongs to through a substring. 3.0.4 additionally equates a `byte` part with an Encoding Object whose `headers` field carries a Content-Transfer-Encoding schema requiring base64; this specification reads that equivalence as declaration semantics, so no such header is emitted for an artifact that does not declare one. [CO30-03: caller input re-keyed to {parameters?, body?}.]
An unknown caller-envelope top-level key refuses before dispatch; only parameters and body are admitted.
A present non-object parameters member refuses before dispatch.
An unknown key inside the parameters member refuses before dispatch.
A cross-location name collision activates qualified mode for every parameter, so the bare name refuses before dispatch.
A well-formed caller envelope supplies colliding path and query parameters through their qualified keys and dispatches successfully.
A deepObject member value containing its structural ampersand delimiter refuses instead of percent-encoding the ambiguity.
The unified resolved-declaration proof follows $ref and allOf and excludes a form-style object member that declares only an object compound shape.
A schema-form Header Parameter value containing CR/LF refuses before an HTTP field is constructed.
A caller-selected request Content-Encoding is governed by the effective Header Parameter, but an unsupported coding token refuses before dispatch rather than being skipped or sniffed.
An actual response Content-Encoding with no governing Header Object is a response protocol error even when the response media declaration otherwise matches.
A governing non-Content-Type response Header Object declaring required true makes the actual header mandatory; absence is a loud response protocol error even for an empty body.
A non-empty response without Content-Type assumes application/octet-stream before ordinary declaration matching and crosses the raw boundary as canonical Base64.
A non-empty actual response with no governing Response Object is a loud protocol error; another status declaration cannot govern it.
A text/event-stream response remains unary under this binding: one HTTP body produces one application string rather than a predecessor streaming sequence.
The identity content-coding is governed but needs no configured codec: request and response stacks preserve the representation bytes unchanged.

Two concrete request-media entries preserve both declared alternatives, but the sole-concrete rule requires configuration.requestMedia before a required body can consume input; examples and supplied value shape select neither.
readOnly and writeOnly are application annotations: the binding preserves both supplied JSON members on the request wire instead of deleting either one.

The usable-set election floor: after the normalized collision makes both application/json spellings unusable, application/vnd.safe+json is the map's exactly-one USABLE concrete alternative and self-selects with no requestMedia configuration, per the amended sole-concrete gloss (exactly one usable entry self-selects; supplied values never elect). [Pins the ratified usable-set election ruling.]

A consumer-supplied Server Variable value outside the declaration's nonempty enum refuses before dispatch; a complete configured URL is the distinct replacement lane, not permission to weaken the selected Server Object.
A query-bearing Server URL excludes the selected target before dispatch because Section 10 defines verbatim path append but no Server-query concatenation cell.
A fragment-bearing Server URL excludes the selected target before dispatch; a fragment never survives as an inferred target-base suffix.

A complete configured URL replaces only the resolved server base: the authored trailing slash and operation's leading path slash remain a double slash, while path substitution and query construction remain unchanged.
Two complete security alternatives require an explicit configuration.security choice even when runtime credentials could satisfy both; artifact order creates no preference and nothing dispatches.
An effective empty security array is a complete no-security alternative: it self-selects, dispatches, and never volunteers unrelated runtime credential material.
A query apiKey comes only from runtime credential context, never the caller envelope, and every reserved, space, and non-ASCII UTF-8 byte is percent-encoded under Section 8.2.
An apiKey cookie value containing a semicolon is not an RFC 6265 cookie-value; it refuses before dispatch and is never percent-encoded into an invented recovery.
A credential/header-parameter collision makes only that security alternative unusable; explicitly selecting the non-colliding alternative emits only its credential and dispatches.
Raw-Cookie and structured-cookie declarations alone exclude nothing: when the invocation supplies only the structured cookie parameter, the operation completes and emits that cookie.
With the same raw-Cookie and structured-cookie declarations, supplying both values refuses before dispatch rather than parsing or merging the raw Cookie string.
A required requestBody declaration on GET is ignored by the 3.0 method-disposition rule: no body input is required and no body or Content-Type is emitted.
Supplying body on GET refuses before dispatch even when the ignored 3.0 requestBody declaration would otherwise describe it.

Accept, Content-Type, and Authorization Header Parameter declarations are ignored only as parameters: artifact-selected body media still emits Content-Type, a selected apiKey credential may emit Authorization, and no Accept field is invented.
A supplied JSON number on a 3.0 schema-form Parameter refuses when parameterConversion is not configured; no canonical numeric spelling is inferred.
A whole JSON null on the 3.0 form-query style path uses the corrected undefined cell and emits q= rather than disappearing or entering parameterConversion.
A null member of a supplied 3.0 array Parameter has no RFC 6570 member representation and refuses before dispatch.
A selected 3.0 Parameter Object declaring both schema and content is excluded before caller values are inspected.
A 3.0 path Parameter whose name has no corresponding path-template expression excludes the selected target.
A supplied empty string for a query Parameter with allowEmptyValue true emits a present zero-length q value; absence and empty remain distinct.
A 3.0 form-style exploded cookie whose resolved declaration proves an array is statically excluded because it produces multiple cookie pairs.
A typeless 3.0 exploded cookie survives static proof, but a supplied array that actually produces multiple pairs refuses at invocation time.
A 3.0 nullable string declaration still has string as its sole non-null type and therefore admits the text/plain character-data lane.
An application/xml media alternative governed by an object declaration is excluded because the OAS XML Object does not determine complete document bytes.
A supplied 3.0 nullable property on the content-based form-urlencoded path is elided as an omitted optional member and contributes no field.
An explicit 3.0 Encoding style selects the RFC 6570 path, where a supplied nullable primitive follows the form-style undefined cell and emits note= instead of being blanket-elided.
Encoding style, explode, and allowReserved are ignored for 3.0 multipart: an object property remains one JSON part under its property name rather than becoming RFC 6570 fields.
A format byte multipart part with an explicit Encoding Content-Transfer-Encoding Header schema admitting base64 emits exactly Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64.
A format byte multipart part whose explicit Encoding Content-Transfer-Encoding Header schema disallows base64 refuses when that part would be emitted.
A relative Server URL declared in an external Path Item resolves against that containing document before the operation path is appended verbatim.
configuration.implicitConnectionScope=referring resolves a 3.0 Security Requirement name in the external document containing the selected operation rather than the entry document.
A nonempty requirement array for a 3.0 non-OAuth scheme makes only that security alternative unusable, so an explicitly selected empty-array alternative still dispatches.
A supplied JSON number for a 3.0 content-based form property refuses when parameterConversion is not configured; the form lane has no partial canonicalization fallback.
A 3.0 root webhooks spelling creates no binding behavior: the selected paths operation remains independently invocable and dispatches no reverse dependency.
A non-transfer Encoding Header Object is descriptive at the 3.0 operation boundary: it neither requires caller input nor makes the multipart alternative unusable.

Two Paths keys with equivalent templated hierarchies but different template names are an OAS-forbidden declaration defect: each selected operation on a participating Path Item is excluded before any caller value is inspected, even though every other declaration on that operation is intact and a non-conflicting sibling path is declared alongside it.

The equivalent-hierarchy exclusion is confined to the participating Path Items: a non-conflicting sibling path declared in the same Paths Object still resolves and dispatches, so the defect never reaches the whole source.

A Responses member that is not a Response Object at all — here a string where the Response Object goes — is an upstream-invalid governing Response Object: it excludes the selected target before any actual response is inspected, and never refuses the whole source.

A governing Response Object whose `links` fixed field carries a value that is not a map violates the Response Object's fixed-field constraints and excludes the selected target before dispatch, exactly as a missing `description` does.

The upstream-invalid Response Object exclusion is confined to the target that owns it: a sibling operation declared in the same Paths Object still resolves and dispatches, so a Response Object the typed loader cannot represent never reaches the whole source.

The upstream-invalid Response Object exclusion reaches the Response Object GOVERNING a successful response. A defect in a declaration that can never govern a 2xx — here an exact 404 — destroys no representation, because a failure body is opaque application-authored data, so the target whose success path is intact still resolves and dispatches.

A request selection made through a range-keyed declaration emits the concrete requestMedia choice that instantiated it as the request Content-Type, never the range key, which names no concrete representation (§9.1's Content-Type emission pin).

The emitted request Content-Type is the elected media type in its parsed form: type and subtype are emitted in lowercase whatever spelling the declaration key used. Which spelling matched never changes the emitted bytes (§9.1's emitted-spelling pin, RFC 9110 §8.3.1).

Every media-type parameter name is emitted in lowercase and each parameter value is emitted in the characters the declaration supplied AFTER unquoting, re-quoted only where the token production does not admit it; utf-8 is a token, so the quoted declaration value emits unquoted (§9.1's emitted-spelling pin over RFC 9110 §§5.6.6, 8.3.1).

A media-type parameter other than charset compares by exact character sequence, so a case-differing requestMedia choice matches no declaration and the unmatched choice refuses before dispatch. RFC 9110 §5.6.6 leaves parameter-value case sensitivity to each parameter's own definition and RFC 2046 §4.1.2 marks charset as the only exception (§9.1's parameter-comparison pin).

A multipart entity is framed under RFC 9110 §8.3.3 and RFC 2046 §5.1.1: the emitted media type carries the generated boundary parameter, each part carries Content-Disposition: form-data with the schema-property name as a QUOTED-STRING, only CRLF represents a line break between body parts, and the entity closes with CRLF, two hyphens, the boundary value and a final two hyphens (§9.3's entity-framing rule and its quoted-name pin).

A successful response whose single Content-Type field value is a LIST of media types selects no media type and is a loud protocol error. RFC 9110 §8.3 defines Content-Type as a single media-type and defines no resolution for the list shape, and the application/octet-stream assumption is granted only for an ABSENT field (§9.5's repeated/list-valued Content-Type rule). The loud protocol error surfaces portably as generic unsuccessful completion, ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED: no more specific code is owned by a governing rule (error-code ownership ruling, 2026-08-31).

On an UNSUCCESSFUL response the same list-valued Content-Type matches no governing content declaration, so the best-effort failure-body rule yields no failure-data value and raises no loud protocol error: the interaction simply completes unsuccessfully (§9.5's repeated/list-valued Content-Type rule, second limb).

A JSON-lane number carrying more precision than binary64 holds never fails or refuses for precision alone: §9.2's permitted set has exactly two members, preserving the supplied mathematical value or reducing it to the nearest binary64 value, and refusal is in neither. The corpus carriage itself reduces the literal, so this scenario pins the no-refusal half of that set rather than discriminating its two members.

A supplied array with ZERO members is an undefined value under RFC 6570 §2.3 — 'A variable defined as a list value is considered undefined if the list contains zero members' — and therefore uses the effective style's undefined cell, which for form is ?color= read under §8.2's presentational-prefix rule (§8.2's three-member undefined-value pin, second member).

A supplied object with ZERO members is an undefined value under RFC 6570 §2.3 — 'an associative array ... is considered undefined if the array contains zero members' — and uses the same form undefined cell (§8.2's three-member undefined-value pin, third member).

The undefined cell is looked up by the effective style, not fixed to one spelling: an empty array on a matrix path parameter emits the matrix undefined cell ';name' rather than form's 'name=' (§8.2's undefined-value rules against the OAS 3.0.4 Style Examples table).

The n/a-cell refusal reaches EVERY undefined value and not JSON null alone: spaceDelimited with explode false is a supported combination whose array column carries real bytes but whose undefined column is n/a, so a supplied empty array refuses before dispatch at that parameter (§8.2's undefined-value n/a rule, generalized from null by the chain-trace repair).

A Schema Object default documents what the receiver assumes and is never inserted by this binding: an unsupplied optional parameter carrying a default is omitted before serialization exactly as one carrying none, so no query component appears at all (§8.1's default-never-inserted rule).

The same default-never-inserted rule holds inside a request body: an object property carrying a default that the caller did not supply is not synthesized into the emitted JSON value (§8.1's default-never-inserted rule at a §9.2 JSON-lane body).

A location-only entry document passes the SAME §3.1 grammar gate as string content: the multi-document YAML stream §3.1 refuses is refused at load when it arrives by dereference rather than embedded. §5.1's retrieval-decode pin states the scope as every retrieval and not the secondary ones alone.

openapi: 3.0.4
info:
  title: T
  version: '1'
servers:
  - url: https://api.example
paths:
  /x:
    get:
      responses:
        '204':
          description: ok
---
second: document

scenarios.description: OAS states normatively that keys used in YAML maps MUST be limited to a scalar string as defined by the YAML Failsafe schema ruleset, and section 3.1 now follows it: the Failsafe ruleset's only scalar tag is tag:yaml.org,2002:str, so every scalar key satisfies the qualifier, an unquoted Responses key is the string it spells, and the document loads. This is the common OpenAPI YAML idiom; the earlier reading refused it.

source.content:
openapi: 3.0.4
info:
  title: T
  version: '1'
servers:
  - url: https://api.example
paths:
  /x:
    get:
      responses:
        204:
          description: ok

scenarios.description: The quoted-key pair of the preceding scenario: an explicitly quoted Responses key is a scalar string under any ruleset, so it loads and dispatches. Together the pair pins that quoting is optional rather than load-bearing, which is what following the edition's Failsafe key rule means.

source.content:
openapi: 3.0.4
info:
  title: T
  version: '1'
servers:
  - url: https://api.example
paths:
  /x:
    get:
      responses:
        '204':
          description: ok

scenarios.description: Elective retrieval on a content-carrying source is never observable: content remains the interpreted artifact and is never silently replaced, so a processor that dereferences the co-present location and one that declines differ in no result this specification defines. The location here answers with a DIFFERENT artifact naming another server; the completed target still comes from content (§4's composition rule).

A selector reaching no addressable target DOES NOT RESOLVE and the invocation refuses AT RESOLUTION — the outcome §3.2's vocabulary added, distinct from an addressable target that is unusable, because no target is reached at all. The path exists and the method does not.

The operation's path bytes append VERBATIM to the expanded Server URL, with no relative URL resolution, no slash normalization and no path repair: a Server URL ending in a slash and a path key beginning with one produce two adjacent slashes in the completed target (§10's verbatim-append pin).

A Security Scheme Object that is not one — here an apiKey declaration missing the REQUIRED name its type demands — excludes every security alternative naming it BEFORE any runtime credential is inspected. Every remaining complete alternative survives, so the sibling alternative is left sole and selects itself (§11's Security Scheme Object required-field exclusion).

A target left with no complete alternative after that exclusion is itself excluded under §3.2's smallest-owner rule, and a selector naming an excluded target still resolves while the invocation refuses before dispatch (§11's Security Scheme Object required-field exclusion against §3.2's exclusion rule).

Accept is on the credential-collision list although §9.1 emits none: emitting no Accept is this specification's decision about response-media negotiation, not a free field, so an apiKey credential destined for it makes the selected alternative unusable and the sole-alternative invocation refuses before dispatch (§11's credential-destination collision rule).

A supplied request value at a raw-octet boundary that is not a JSON string refuses before dispatch at the affected body; the value never reaches the wire in a repaired form (§9.2's raw-octet boundary rule).

A supplied raw-octet string that §9.2's canonical RFC 4648 §4 reading does not decode — here a one-character quantum with neither the required padding nor a whole group — refuses before dispatch rather than being repaired or partially decoded (§9.2's raw-octet boundary rule).
A plain scalar key never refuses on its resolved type, whichever Core-schema tag that resolution assigns: an unquoted true in key position is the member name it spells, and the document loads.

source.content:
openapi: 3.0.4
info:
  title: T
  version: '1'
servers:
  - url: https://api.example
x-vendor:
  true: 1
paths:
  /x:
    get:
      responses:
        '204':
          description: ok

scenarios.description: What refuses at the key gate is a key that is no scalar at all. A sequence in key position is no representation of a JSON member name and refuses at load.
